context: You're a construction foreman. A skilled crew member keeps skipping safety steps to work faster.
option_a: Cut him loose — one accident risks everyone, and standards can't bend for talent.
option_b: Keep and coach him hard — real skill is rare, and discipline can be taught.

context: You're a nurse on a short-staffed ward. A dying patient asks you to skip a noisy protocol so his last hours are peaceful.
option_a: Honor his wish — comfort and dignity matter more than the checklist now.
option_b: Follow the protocol — the rules exist for moments exactly this fraught.

context: You run a small shop. A loyal employee of ten years has been underperforming badly for a year.
option_a: Keep them — loyalty is a two-way street, and you don't discard people.
option_b: Let them go — the business carries everyone, and it can't carry deadweight.

context: You're an electrician. A customer wants a cheaper shortcut that isn't up to code but would probably be fine.
option_a: Refuse — your name is on the work, and 'probably fine' is how people get hurt.
option_b: Do it their way — it's their house, their money, and their risk to take.

context: You're a chef at the dinner rush. A plate comes up just slightly imperfect.
option_a: Send it — the table is waiting, and good-enough on time beats perfect too late.
option_b: Remake it — every plate carries your name; you don't serve 'just slightly' anything.

context: You're a retail manager setting the holiday schedule. A single parent and a reliable ten-year veteran both want the same days off.
option_a: Give it to the parent — need should weigh more than tenure.
option_b: Give it to the veteran — earned seniority is the fairest rule you've got.

context: You're a social worker. A struggling parent loves their kid but keeps slipping. You can remove the child or give one more chance.
option_a: Give another chance — a flawed home with love beats the trauma of removal.
option_b: Remove the child — your first duty is the child's safety, not the parent's hope.
axis: preserve the family vs protect the child

context: You're a long-haul trucker behind schedule. You're tired enough that you should stop, but stopping loses the on-time bonus.
option_a: Pull over — no delivery is worth your life or someone else's on the road.
option_b: Push through — you know your limits, and the bonus is real money you need.

context: You're a bartender. A regular who tips well has clearly had enough.
option_a: Cut him off — your call, your responsibility, no matter how good a customer.
option_b: Serve him one more — he's a grown man, harmless, and it's not your job to parent him.
axis: duty of care vs personal autonomy

context: You're a farmer in a dry year. Sell the herd now at a loss, or gamble that the rains come.
option_a: Sell now — cut the loss you can see rather than bet the farm on weather.
option_b: Hold the line — you've weathered dry years before, and panic sells cheap.

context: You're a factory line lead. A defect slips through. Stopping the line is costly; letting it ride risks more bad units.
option_a: Stop the line — a problem caught is cheap; a problem shipped is expensive.
option_b: Let it run — one defect isn't worth halting everyone; flag it and fix it downstream.
axis: halt for quality vs keep flow

context: You're a hair stylist. A client asks for a cut you're sure will look bad on them.
option_a: Give them what they asked for — it's their head and their choice to make.
option_b: Talk them out of it — they're paying for your eye, not just your scissors.

context: You own a small business and can give a raise that would genuinely strain cash flow, or hold off.
option_a: Give the raise — people are loyal to bosses who are generous when it's hard.
option_b: Hold off — a raise you can't sustain helps no one if it sinks the company.

context: You're a firefighter at a partly-collapsed building. Someone might be trapped inside.
option_a: Go in — the whole point of the job is the chance someone's still alive.
option_b: Hold for the team — a dead rescuer saves no one; discipline beats heroics.

context: You're a restaurant owner with a star chef whose food is incredible but who is cruel to the kitchen staff.
option_a: Keep the chef — the food is why people come, and talent earns some rope.
option_b: Fire the chef — no plate is worth a kitchen full of people who dread the shift.

context: You're a mechanic. Fixing the car, you spot a separate problem the customer didn't ask about.
option_a: Mention only what they came for — don't upsell people who didn't ask.
option_b: Flag everything you see — they trust you to be their eyes under the hood.

context: You're a teacher. A gifted student who has lied before claims a real emergency the morning of the final exam.
option_a: Let them retake it — if you're wrong to refuse, the cost to them is too high.
option_b: Hold the line — rules that bend for the clever stop being rules.

context: You're a paramedic. A family begs you to break protocol so their dying mother passes more gently.
option_a: Bend for them — at the very end, comfort outweighs the rulebook.
option_b: Hold to protocol — it's there precisely so grief doesn't drive the call.

context: You're a union rep at the bargaining table. Push for the maximum raise and risk some jobs, or take a modest deal that protects everyone.
option_a: Push hard — you fight for the best, and timidity leaves money on the table.
option_b: Take the safe deal — a smaller raise everyone keeps beats a big one that costs jobs.

context: You're a carpenter. The client's budget forces a corner you'd rather not cut.
option_a: Do it within budget — meeting people where they are is part of the craft.
option_b: Insist on doing it right — you won't put your name on work you know is compromised.

context: You manage a warehouse under quota pressure. One worker is steady but slow and clearly struggling to keep pace.
option_a: Push the numbers — the team's targets protect everyone's jobs, including theirs.
option_b: Protect the person — burn out a good worker and you've solved nothing.

context: You're a butcher. A regular wants a cheaper cut wrapped and sold to his guests as the premium one.
option_a: Refuse the deception — your counter runs on honesty, and that's not for sale.
option_b: Do it — he's a grown man spending his own money on his own dinner party.

context: You're a fire captain choosing who to promote: the bold one who takes risks and gets results, or the careful one who never loses anyone.
option_a: Promote the bold one — the job needs nerve, and results speak.
option_b: Promote the careful one — leadership is keeping everyone alive, not heroics.

context: You're a night-shift security guard. You find a hungry teenager who's broken in to sleep somewhere warm.
option_a: By the book — call it in; rules don't bend just because the story is sad.
option_b: Show mercy — feed the kid, send them off, and forget you saw anything.

context: You're a hotel housekeeper and find a thick roll of cash left behind in a checked-out room.
option_a: Turn it in — it isn't yours, full stop, no matter who left it.
option_b: Keep it — it was abandoned, you're underpaid, and finders keepers.

context: You're a coach in a championship season. Your star is nursing an injury that could worsen if they play.
option_a: Play them — this is the moment everyone trained for; you go for the title.
option_b: Rest them — protect the athlete's whole career over one trophy.
axis: win now vs the long game

context: You're a startup founder. Ship the rough product now and catch the market window, or polish it and risk missing the moment.
option_a: Ship it — a real product in the world beats a perfect one that's late.
option_b: Polish it — your first impression is the one people remember; don't waste it.
axis: speed to market vs first-impression quality

context: You're a charge nurse. A beloved, excellent colleague cut one corner that could have hurt a patient.
option_a: Report it by the book — a good record can't buy a pass on patient safety.
option_b: Handle it quietly — a private word fixes it without ending a great career.
axis: by the book vs protect a good person

context: You're a landscaper. The client wants a striking plant you know is invasive and will spread to the neighbors.
option_a: Give them the look they want — it's their yard and their decision.
option_b: Steer them away — you won't plant something you know will become everyone's problem.

context: You're a flight attendant. A passenger is breaking a minor rule, harmlessly, and enforcing it will make a scene.
option_a: Enforce it — small rules hold because everyone keeps them, scene or not.
option_b: Let it slide — a calm cabin matters more than a pointless point of principle.
